scope: Supplementary Linux x64 FILE stream-state comparisons and existing filesystem regressions. Not a full upstream-suite or cross-platform result. No original upstream test or expected output was edited.
findings: A final unterminated getLine left EOF set and concealed appended data on the next line or byte read.
getdelim can return partial data with ferror set, and refuses to consume further bytes when a prior stream error remains set; native Lean consumes through its getc loop and then reports the error.
Native Handle.read prioritizes EOF over a sticky error when fread returns zero and clears both flags.
implementation: Preserve native per-operation error/EOF ordering. Keep getdelim for ordinary streams and use getc behavior when an earlier error remains set. No Lean API or syntax changes.

The first native C fixture coupled its final EOF check to earlier line results. Its failures are retained. The refined fixture uses an independent pipe for byte-reader EOF ordering; it fails before and passes after the repair in all three engines.
The C control follows the operation order in pinned Lean runtime/io.cpp. It also verifies which bytes remain after the sticky-error call, not only whether an error is returned.
